title: Categorical Prior Lock-in: Why In-Context Learning Fails for Structured Data
summary: This paper studies why in-context learning with large language models fails to reproduce categorical distributions in structured/tabular data generation, identifying a failure mode called 'categorical prior lock-in' where LLMs cannot update pre-trained token priors even when conditioned on new examples. It contrasts this with parameter-efficient fine-tuning (LoRA), which fixes the distributional mismatch but introduces memorization risk. CTGAN is cited in the related-work section as the dominant pre-LLM GAN-based baseline, described for its conditional generator and mode-specific normalization but not run in the experiments.
evidence: "CTGAN [11] addresses mixed column types and class imbalance through a conditional generator and mode-specific normalization, establishing a widely-used baseline." — described in related work, not run in experiments.

title: Causal Analysis of Social Support on Functional Outcomes in Stroke Rehabilitation: A Study Using Synthetic Data and Advanced Inference Methods
summary: This medRxiv preprint applies causal inference methods (propensity scores, TMLE) to a synthetic stroke rehabilitation dataset to test whether high social support causally affects functional outcomes 12 months post-stroke, finding no significant effect once depression is adjusted for as a confounder. The synthetic dataset underlying the entire analysis was generated using SDV's Gaussian Copula Synthesizer and assessed with SDV's evaluation framework, achieving a 95.75% overall quality score. SDV's GaussianCopula synthesizer is run as the generator producing the synthetic data the whole causal analysis rests on, with its quality report used to validate fidelity.
evidence: "This synthetic data was generated using the Gaussian Copula Synthesizer, a feature of the Synthetic Data Vault (SDV) library [14]... The generated synthetic data achieved a high quality score of 95.75% according to the SDV evaluation framework."

title: Causal Data Augmentation for Robust Fine-Tuning of Tabular Foundation Models
summary: This NeurIPS 2025 workshop paper proposes CausalMixFT, a method that fits Structural Causal Models on scarce target-dataset samples to generate structurally consistent synthetic examples for fine-tuning tabular foundation models, improving validation-based early stopping and downstream performance across 33 TabArena classification datasets. The authors compare their causal generator against several purely statistical synthetic-data augmentation baselines. CTGAN is run as one of several baseline generators (fit via a hyperparameter search including embedding_dim and related constructor parameters), and its mode-specific normalization approach is used to produce comparison synthetic data that CausalMixFT is shown to outperform.

evidence: "outperforming purely statistical generators such as CTGAN (-0.01), TabEBM (-0.04), and TableAugment (-0.09)"; hyperparameter table lists CTGANGenerator params including embedding_dim, confirming the sdv-dev package was run.

title: Causal Parametric Drift Simulation: A Digital Twin Framework for Classifier Robustness Evaluation
summary: This paper proposes a Digital Twin framework using Structural Causal Models to simulate causal parametric drift for stress-testing classifier robustness, applied to the OSMI mental-health dataset and evaluated against statistical drift monitors and SHAP-based explanations. CTGAN is cited only briefly in the related-work discussion of deep generative models that achieve high-fidelity sampling of P(X,Y) but lack controlled causal interventions, contrasting with the authors' causal SCM approach. CTGAN is mentioned as a black-box generative baseline paradigm the paper positions itself against, but it is neither run nor benchmarked.
evidence: "Deep generative models such as GANs ... and VAEs ... achieve high fidelity in sampling P(X,Y) (Xu et al., 2019), but operate as black boxes with entangled latent spaces that preclude controlled interventions."

title: Causal-Privacy Audit Workflow for Synthetic and Distilled Data in Dropout Support
summary: This paper introduces CaP-Eval, a decision-facing causal-privacy audit workflow that compares original, distilled, adversarial-synthetic, statistical-synthetic (Gaussian Copula), and differentially-private (DPGNet) student data on predictive utility, treatment-effect fidelity, estimator robustness, and privacy-governance risk, using a university dropout dataset with financial-status covariates. It finds that DPGNet and distilled data preserve causal treatment-effect structure more reliably than the SDV-based adversarial and Gaussian Copula baselines, which attenuate effect magnitudes. SDV's CTGAN-based synthesizer and its GaussianCopula synthesizer are both run through SDV's metadata workflow as two of the several generated-data baselines evaluated in the audit.

title: CausalDiffTab: Mixed-Type Causal-Aware Diffusion for Tabular Data Generation
summary: This preprint introduces CausalDiffTab, a diffusion-model-based generator for mixed-type tabular data (numerical and categorical) that adds a hybrid adaptive causal regularization method to improve fidelity without sacrificing generative quality, evaluated across seven benchmark datasets against nine baseline synthesizers. CTGAN and TVAE, both from the SDV-family CTGAN paper, are run as two of the nine baseline methods for comparison on shape/trend fidelity, privacy (DCR), and downstream ML utility metrics. SDV's CTGAN (mode-specific normalization) and TVAE are benchmarked against, not extended, in this evaluation.

title: Data-centric AI: Perspectives and Challenges
summary: This is a survey/position paper that maps out data-centric AI (DCAI) as a field, organizing techniques into training data development, inference data development, and data maintenance, and outlining open challenges for the research community. It does not run any experiments itself but cites prior work exemplifying each technique category. title: CGGM: A conditional graph generation model with adaptive sparsity for node anomaly detection in IoT networks
summary: This paper proposes CGGM, a GAN-based conditional graph generation model that integrates network topology with multi-dimensional node features to generate balanced synthetic traffic graph snapshots for anomaly detection in IoT networks, using an adaptive sparsity adjacency generator, a multi-head self-attention feature encoder, and a distribution-distance latent constraint. It is evaluated against graph-based baselines (GraphRNN, GraphSGAN) and tabular data generation baselines on UNSW-NB15 and CICIDS-2017 datasets. CTGAN is run as one of two tabular-data-generation baselines, compared on classification performance, T-SNE visualization, and Wasserstein/MMD/KSTest distribution-discrepancy metrics against the proposed CGGM model.

title: ciDATGAN: Conditional Inputs for Tabular GANs
summary: This technical report proposes ciDATGAN, an evolution of the authors' own Directed Acyclic Tabular GAN (DATGAN) that adds conditional inputs inspired by image-completion methods, and shows it can be used to debias datasets and complete large synthetic populations from a smaller feeder dataset. In its related-work discussion of tabular GANs, the paper describes CTGAN's introduction of conditionality via concatenation and notes it demonstrates the conditional vector is critical for imbalanced datasets, without providing specific conditionality results itself. CTGAN's conditional vector is discussed as prior art the authors' own DATGAN-based model departs from, but CTGAN is never run in the experiments.
evidence: "CTGAN (Xu et al., 2019) introduces conditionality for tabular GANs using concatenation. While they show that the conditional vector is critical for imbalanced datasets, they do not provide specific results on the conditionality."

title: Class-Dependent Hybrid Data Augmentation for Multiclass Migraine Classification under Severe Class Imbalance
summary: This paper reproduces and corrects prior migraine subtype classification studies for data leakage and metric bias, then proposes a class-dependent hybrid augmentation framework that assigns Gaussian Copula to small classes and CTGAN to larger classes, plus a 'fidelity asymmetry' concept for proportionally constrained synthetic growth. Evaluated on a 400-patient, seven/six-subtype clinical dataset with eight classifiers under stratified 5-fold cross-validation, the hybrid strategy outperforms single-method augmenters in macro-F1. SDV is run directly as the generator for both the Gaussian Copula and CTGAN synthesizers underpinning the entire augmentation pipeline, with CTGAN hyperparameters (epochs, batch_size, pac, generator_dim, discriminator_dim) also reported and TVAE included as an additional comparison generator.

title: ClavaDDPM: Multi-relational Data Synthesis with Cluster-guided Diffusion Models
summary: This paper proposes ClavaDDPM, a diffusion-model-based approach for synthesizing multi-relational (multi-table) data that uses clustering labels as intermediaries to propagate learned latent variables across tables via foreign-key relationships, aiming to capture long-range dependencies that prior methods miss. It is evaluated against PrivLava and other multi-table baselines on datasets of varying size and complexity. SDV's HMA-based Gaussian-copula relational synthesizer is run as one of the primary multi-relational baselines, and CTGAN is run as a single-table backbone model within comparison pipelines (ST-CTGAN, D-CTGAN).
evidence: "We adopt two multi-relational synthesis models in literature as our baselines: PrivLava [5] ... and SDV [35] as a statistical method specially designed for multi-relational synthesis." and "For these two pipelines, we use CTGAN [47] and TabDDPM [25] as the single-table backbone models."

title: Close to Reality: Interpretable and Feasible Data Augmentation for Imbalanced Learning
summary: This preprint introduces DPG-da, a data-augmentation framework that extracts interpretable decision predicates from trained models to enforce domain constraints during over-sampling, aiming to produce diverse yet feasible and interpretable synthetic minority-class samples. The method is benchmarked against a large set of over-sampling techniques including SMOTE variants, ROS, and generative tabular models across many real-world imbalanced datasets, measuring F1-score and runtime. CTGAN, TVAE, and CopulaGAN (from the SDV library) are run unmodified as three of twelve baseline over-sampling methods compared against DPG-da.
evidence: "generative approaches for tabular data (CTGAN, TVAE, COPULA-GAN) and ROS. Baselines were run with standard hyperparameters to ensure fair comparison." — CTGAN, TVAE and COPULA-GAN appear as three of twelve oversampling baselines in the critical-difference and runtime comparisons against the proposed DPG-da method.

title: CoDi: Co-evolving Contrastive Diffusion Models for Mixed-type Tabular Synthesis
summary: This paper proposes CoDi, two co-evolving conditional diffusion models with contrastive training that process continuous and discrete tabular columns separately yet jointly, aiming to better preserve inter-column correlations than prior tabular synthesis methods. It is evaluated against 8 baseline generators (including MedGAN, VEEGAN, TableGAN, OCT-GAN, RNODE, STaSy, CTGAN and TVAE) across 11 real-world datasets on quality, diversity, and sampling-time metrics. CTGAN and TVAE are run throughout as two of several comparison baselines, while SDV's Patki et al. (2016) recursive Gaussian-copula table modeling is cited only in the related-work discussion as prior art.

title: CoMedBench: A Multi-Source Benchmark of Synthetic Medical Data Fidelity and Downstream Utility
summary: CoMedBench is a reproducible benchmark evaluating a family of synthetic-data generators across 37 tabular and temporal downstream clinical-prediction tasks drawn from seven public healthcare data sources (MIMIC-III/IV, eICU, UCI, NHANES, BRFSS, pycox). It compares statistical fidelity and downstream utility of CTGAN-, TVAE-, CopulaGAN-, and GaussianCopula-based generators (named CoMed-CTGAN, CoMed-TVAE, CoMed-CopulaGAN, CoMed-GaussianCopula) trained on the same data. SDV's CTGAN, TVAE, CopulaGAN and GaussianCopula synthesizers are run directly as the four generators whose fidelity and downstream utility form the entire empirical comparison.

summary: This paper compares SynDiffix, a new anonymization-focused multi-table synthetic data generator, against 15 other commercial and academic synthetic data techniques using the SDNIST analysis framework, evaluating utility and privacy across low- and high-dimensional measures. CTGAN is included as one of the 15 benchmarked techniques, credited to SDV and cited to the CTGAN paper, run as an evaluation subject rather than as the paper's own method. SDV's CTGAN is run as one of several baseline generative models compared against SynDiffix on accuracy, PCA error, and inconsistency metrics.

title: COMPASS: A Unified Decision-Intelligence System for Navigating Performance Trade-off in HPC
summary: COMPASS is a modular, interactive decision-intelligence engine for HPC configuration selection that turns user queries (recommend, reconfigure, what-if) into ML tasks, quantifies the trustworthiness of its suggestions, and is validated against analytical ground truth, published findings, and real hardware. It is compared against autotuners, predictive models, and generative modeling baselines including CTGAN, GAN, GReaT, and diffusion models on tabular configuration generation tasks. CTGAN is run as one of several generative baselines in the paper's comparison table, evaluated against COMPASS on recommendation quality, training/inference speed, and reconstruction accuracy.

title: Composable Generative Models
summary: This preprint introduces the Composable Generative Model (CGM), a transformer-based autoregressive architecture in which any conditional generative sub-model can be nested to jointly generate heterogeneous tabular data (numerical, categorical, image, text, sequence) with privacy-preserving applications in mind. The authors evaluate CGM against 14 recent generative models across 13 datasets using the public SDGym benchmark and leaderboard, reporting it beats prior tabular generators including CTGAN, TVAE and CopulaGAN. SDGym is run directly as the benchmarking harness, and CTGAN/TVAE/CopulaGAN (SDV-family synthesizers) serve as the baseline models CGM is compared against on likelihood and ML-efficacy metrics.

title: Comprehensive monitoring of tissue composition using in vivo imaging of cell nuclei and deep learning
summary: This preprint introduces NuCLear, a method combining in vivo two-photon imaging of histone 2B-eGFP-labeled cell nuclei with a deep-learning classifier to identify and localize brain cell types (neurons, astrocytes, microglia, oligodendrocytes, endothelial cells) non-invasively over time in mouse cortex. To balance the number of training examples across cell types, the authors used the Synthetic Data Vault (SDV) package to generate synthetic nuclei feature datasets exploiting correlations, means, extrema and standard deviations of the original features, achieving about 83% fidelity to the original data distribution.

CTGAN's conditional generator design is discussed in prose as prior work, not run or benchmarked in this survey.

summary: This preprint surveys generative diffusion models applied to structured data, covering tabular and time series data across data-driven general tasks and domain-specific applications such as EHR generation, forecasting, biosignal enhancement, and recommendation systems. It reviews prior deep generative approaches (VAE, GAN) before diving into diffusion model theory and cataloguing dozens of diffusion-based methods across these domains. summary: This preprint extends TCAV (Testing with Concept Activation Vectors) from image models to tabular deep learning, proposing a way to define human-interpretable concepts over table rows and a TCAV-based fairness notion linked to demographic parity. To generate the concept examples needed for training concept activation vectors, the authors train CTGAN models on subsets of the tabular data (e.g., splitting by an age threshold) and sample synthetic rows from them. CTGAN, the conditional GAN for tabular data described in the SDV-family CTGAN paper, is run as the generator that produces all the concept-example data underlying the paper's experiments.

title: Constrained Adaptive Attack: Effective Adversarial Attack Against Deep Neural Networks for Tabular Data

In their experiments, CT-GAN is considered as one of two data-augmentation techniques (alongside Cutmix) used to defend the tabular models being attacked. CTGAN is cited and applied only as an augmentation baseline against which the paper's attacks are evaluated, with no further engagement with its architecture.

title: On the Constrained Time-Series Generation Problem
summary: This paper addresses generating synthetic time series that are both statistically realistic and satisfy externally imposed numerical constraints, proposing a constrained-optimization framework and a guided diffusion model called 'GuidedDiffTime' that avoids costly retraining or rejection sampling when constraints change. It evaluates the approach on financial and energy time-series datasets, showing improved realism and constraint satisfaction with reduced computational cost. The SDV paper is cited only in passing as an example of the reject-and-resample approach to constraint enforcement, with no SDV code run.

As non-LLM baselines for comparison, the authors generate synthetic tabular data with classical tabular generators including TVAE and CTGAN. CTGAN and TVAE are run as one set of several baseline synthesizers benchmarked against the LLM-based in-context generation approach.

summary: This preprint proposes conditional normalizing flows (cNF) to refine sub-national household survey distributions under severe data scarcity, evaluating across eight humanitarian household survey datasets spanning six low- and middle-income countries. The main inferential results rest on the cNF's ability to condition generation on continuous external covariates, a mechanism the authors argue standard tabular generative models lack. As a supplementary benchmark, CTGAN and TVAE, implemented via the SDV library, are run as unconditional baselines against the cNF, comparing fidelity and originality of synthetic survey data.

summary: This paper introduces HoneyPlotNet, a multi-modal generative system combining a multitask Transformer and a specialized autoencoder to automatically produce realistic charts (captions, plot text, and underlying tabular data) for honeyfiles used in cyber deception. It also releases a new document-chart dataset and a Keyword Semantic Matching metric to evaluate semantic consistency. title: Continuous Diffusion for Mixed-Type Tabular Data
summary: This paper proposes CDTD, a continuous diffusion model for mixed-type tabular data that unifies noise processes for continuous and categorical features via score matching and score interpolation, with adaptive feature- or type-specific noise schedules. It is benchmarked against a suite of tabular generators (SMOTE, ARF, CTGAN, TVAE, TabDDPM, CoDi, TabSyn) across many real-world datasets on distributional, correlation, ML-efficacy and privacy metrics. The authors compare similarity-based (DCR) and attack-based privacy metrics, with and without their embeddings, on synthetic datasets generated by CTGAN, DPCTGAN, and RealTabFormer across three public datasets. CTGAN is run as one of three deep-learning generators used to produce the synthetic data that the privacy metrics are evaluated against.

summary: This paper proposes three new evaluation metrics—FAED, FPCAD, and RFIS—for assessing generative models on tabular data, and stress-tests them against established metrics by injecting Quality Decrease, Mode Drop, and Mode Collapse degradations into three network intrusion detection datasets. Throughout the experiments, SDV's Fidelity metric (via SDMetrics/DataCebo) is run alongside Utility, TSTR, and TRTS as an established baseline and is repeatedly shown to be insensitive to injected data-quality problems compared to the authors' proposed metrics. CTGAN, TGAN, CopulaGAN, and TVAE are also discussed in related work as prior generative architectures but are not run in the experiments. SDV's SDMetrics fidelity/quality-report measure is used as a benchmarked baseline evaluation method that the paper's new metrics are shown to outperform.

title: Evaluating Machine Learning Models for Post-Wildfire Debris-Flow Prediction
summary: This preprint systematically evaluates 15 machine learning models, including the TabPFN foundation model, for predicting post-wildfire debris flows from basin-scale rainfall, burn-severity, and terrain features across the western United States, using SHAP for feature importance and TabPFN-generated synthetic data to address class imbalance and limited training data. The actual synthetic augmentation used is TabPFN, not any SDV-family tool. CTGAN is cited only in the reference list, with no engagement or use of it found anywhere in the body text.

title: Evaluating Privacy-Utility Tradeoffs in Synthetic Smart Grid Data
summary: This preprint benchmarks four synthetic data generation methods—WGAN, CTGAN, a diffusion model, and Gaussian noise augmentation—for producing privacy-preserving smart-meter data used to classify households' suitability for dynamic Time-of-Use electricity tariffs, evaluating classification utility, distribution fidelity, and resistance to reconstruction and membership-inference attacks. CTGAN is run directly via SDV's CTGANSynthesizer with a SingleTableMetadata schema as one of the four generators compared, and its full-synthetic variant is found to offer the strongest privacy protection despite slightly lower utility than diffusion models.

title: Evaluating quality in synthetic data generation for large tabular health datasets
summary: This paper benchmarks seven tabular synthetic data generators (including TVAE, CTGAN, PGM, PrivSyn, TabDDPM, TableDiffusion, and GReaT) across four datasets of varying scale, with systematic hyperparameter optimization for each model-dataset pair. It proposes a methodology for visualizing and quantifying fidelity of synthesized joint distributions and applies it to a domain-specific German Cancer Registries epidemiological dataset, revealing challenges in medical-domain adherence. CTGAN and TVAE are run directly as two of the seven benchmarked synthesizers, with their published hyperparameter ranges (embedding_dim, l2scale, loss_factor, compress_dims, decompress_dims) matching the CTGAN/TVAE implementation from the sdv-dev ecosystem, evaluated as subjects rather than as the paper's own method.

title: Evaluating utility in synthetic banking microdata applications
summary: This preprint develops an evaluation framework for the utility and privacy of synthetic banking microdata, applying it to financial usage indices, term deposit yield curves, and credit card transition matrices using confidential data from the Central Bank of Paraguay. The empirical comparison runs several differentially private synthesizers (MST, AIM, PAC, DPCTGAN, PATECTGAN), finding marginal-based inference methods generally outperform GAN-based ones for these applications. title: Evaluating virtual-control-augmented trials for reproducing treatment effect from original RCTs
summary: This preprint empirically tests whether completing prematurely-stopped control arms of randomized controlled trials with AI-generated 'virtual patients' can reproduce the treatment effect of the original, fully-recruited trial, using data from the IST and IST3 stroke trials. The authors train CTGAN and TVAE on recruited control patients, generate virtual controls to complete partially recruited arms, and show this can produce substantially biased or misleading treatment-effect estimates. Both generative architectures are implemented via the Synthetic Data Vault (SDV) library, with hyperparameters tuned and synthetic data quality assessed using SDMetrics' general score, making SDV's CTGAN and TVAE synthesizers the core generators underpinning the whole empirical study.

title: Evaluation is Key: A Survey on Evaluation Measures for Synthetic Time Series
summary: A survey that catalogues and analyzes measures for evaluating synthetic time-series data, arguing that no consensus exists on evaluation procedures and providing a guide to help researchers select appropriate metrics. It does not propose a new generative model but surveys the evaluation landscape across generative approaches for time series. The SDV-family paper on sequential models (PAR/DeepEcho) appears only in the reference list, with no discussion or engagement in the body text.

title: Evaluation of the Synthetic Electronic Health Records
summary: This preprint proposes two new sample-wise metrics, Similarity and Uniqueness, for evaluating synthetic tabular/EHR data beyond standard downstream-task utility measures, demonstrating them on synthetic Cystic Fibrosis patient records generated by four state-of-the-art generative models (VAE, CTGAN, and two DPGAN privacy variants). CTGAN is implemented as one of the four generators compared across utility, similarity, and uniqueness metrics, with the authors stating they 'attempted to preserve their original architecture' for each model. CTGAN's conditional-vector mechanism for handling sparse, imbalanced categorical columns is described and the model is run as one of several generators benchmarked in the study, though it appears to be the authors' own reimplementation rather than the sdv-dev package.

title: On the evaluation of synthetic longitudinal electronic health records
summary: This preprint discusses and demonstrates methods for evaluating the quality of synthetic longitudinal electronic health records, covering fidelity via low-dimensional projections, a discriminative goodness-of-fit classifier, utility via train-on-synthetic-test-on-real clinical prediction tasks, and privacy risk via attribute inference. The authors apply these metrics to synthetic EHR data generated from the MIMIC-IV dataset using two open-source libraries. SDV's PARSynthesizer (sequential/longitudinal model) is run alongside Gretel-Synthetics to generate the synthetic longitudinal data that the proposed evaluation metrics are then applied to.

title: Explainable and fair anti money laundering models using a reproducible SHAP framework for financial institutions
summary: This preprint proposes an end-to-end pipeline for explainable and fair anti-money-laundering detection, combining synthetic data generation, imbalance-aware classifiers (Random Forest, MLP) with F2-optimized thresholds, and SHAP-based explainability and fairness auditing. The authors construct a 10,000-record synthetic AML dataset with a binary target and extreme class imbalance to evaluate the pipeline under conditions mimicking production AML systems. title: An Explainable AI Model for the Detecting Malicious Smart Contracts Based on EVM Opcode Based Features
summary: This preprint proposes a machine-learning pipeline for detecting malicious Ethereum smart contracts from EVM opcode frequency features, using SMOTE to balance the dataset, entropy-based binning to binarize features, and LIME to explain the classifier's predictions, achieving 99% detection with a 0.01 false positive rate. In the introduction the authors mention a future direction of synthetically generating malicious contracts using a conditional GAN to train an adversarial-resistant classifier, citing the CTGAN paper, but no such generation is implemented or run in the reported experiments (SMOTE is used instead). title: Explanation Design in Strategic Learning: Sufficient Explanations that Induce Non-harmful Responses
summary: This preprint studies how decision makers should design explanations for strategic agents so that agents do not respond in ways that harm their own utility, proving that action-recommendation-based explanations (ARexes) are sufficient for non-harmful responses and proposing a joint learning procedure for the predictive model and explanation policy. In their experiments on synthetic tasks, the authors fit CTGAN on an original dataset to generate additional synthetic training and testing samples used to simulate agent-DM interactions. title: Exploring the Heterogeneity of Tabular Data: A Diversity-aware Data Generator via LLMs
summary: This paper proposes DATE, a diversity-aware tabular data generation framework that partitions heterogeneous tabular data into distributionally distinct subsets and uses LLMs with decision-tree-reasoning feedback and a multi-armed-bandit sampling algorithm to balance diversity and quality of generated data. To build a synthetic population matching the distribution of their real X-ray binary sample for this spatial comparison, the authors use a Conditional Tabular GAN (CTGAN, Xu et al. 2019), a component of the SDV family, run directly as the generator of the synthetic comparison sample.
